newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South African wool prices rise at weekly sale.
newsitem.headline: South African wool prices rise at weekly sale.

text.p: South African wool prices rose at the latest weekly auction, the Wool Board said on Thursday.
Of the total 9,288 bales on offer, 98.3 percent was sold.
Prices for 20 micron rose 1.0 percent, 21 rose 0.9 percent, 22 rose 0.8 pct, 23 fell 0.5 percent, 24 micron rose 1.1 percent and 25 micron rose 0.9 percent.
Bellies rose 0.4 percent, lambs fell 0.2 percent and locks rose 0.6 percent.
The offering included 1,973 bales of merino together with 1,012 other white, 215 bales Ciskei, 539 bales Lesotho and 263 bales of coarse and coloured.
Top-selling wool was 24 and 25 micron which sold 100 pct.
502 bales offered and 99.2 percent of 20 micron sold.
1,316 bales offered and 99.8 percent of 21 micron sold.
1,692 bales offered and 96.9 percent of 22 micron sold.
855 bales offered and 99.2 percent of 24 micron were sold.
351 bales offered and 100.0 percent of 25 micron were sold.
The next sale will be held on January 29 with about 10,000 bales on offer.
